name: Kim Ung Sun

attribution.legal_posture: Current OFAC exact-ID component-table data confirms the administrative-list entry and adds only the bounded structured context stated here. The subject is a DPRK representative tied to the Chinyong/Sinjin IT-worker network and an OFAC-designated DPRK official. Treasury describes Kim Ung Sun as a Russia-based economic and trade consular official who worked with Vitaliy Sergeyevich Andreyev to facilitate cryptocurrency-to-cash transfers supporting Chinyong. This is an OFAC administrative sanctions designation; no criminal charge or conviction appears in the record.

locations: Khabarovsk, Russia (OFAC listing context; not current location)
caveats: Administrative sanctions state an administrative status; criminal charges and convictions require separate proceedings.
Sanctions-list address context is historical location context; present physical location, current operations, ownership, employment, or control require current evidence.
SDN.CSV, ADD.CSV, and ALT.CSV are component tables of one current OFAC dataset and count as one source family.
Street and postal addresses, birth data, passports, government and company identifiers, email addresses, financial selectors, and sanctions boilerplate are excluded.
The city is sanctions-list context; present presence or role requires a current source.
Treasury's description is an administrative sanctions finding; criminal conviction status belongs to a separate court record.

identity_boundary: Kim Ung Sun (김응순), listed by OFAC as KIM, Ung Sun with the alternate romanization KIM, U'ng-sun, is the Russia-based DPRK economic and trade consular official described by Treasury. The source reports coordination connected to payments supporting Chinyong; employment by Chinyong or Korea Sinjin remains unestablished. The record carries the administrative-sanctions posture.
